clue.text: Plot swindles and breach of copyright

parts.note: cons are confidence tricks, so swindles
piracy is the illegal copying of protected work

explanation.surface: A plot involving fraud and illegal copying of protected work.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret scheme hatched by several people is a plot in the sinister sense.

clue.text: Irritable taxi driver having to cross river

indicators.note: crossing places one word across the other, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: a cabby drives a cab

explanation.surface: A grumpy cabbie must drive over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having to cross' puts R inside CABBY.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad-tempered, like a crab, a synonym.

clue.text: Temperament shown by angry EU rant?

indicators.note: angry suggests agitation, so the letters of EU rant are stirred up

explanation.surface: An outburst against the European Union reveals one's character.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's innate character or disposition.

clue.text: Cause of hold-ups at the couturier is a sensation

definitions.text: Cause of hold-ups at the couturier
definitions.meaning: a dressmaker's sharp tools that hold fabric in place
a tingling feeling as a numb limb recovers

explanation.definitionFit: Literally a dressmaker's fixing tools; figuratively the prickly tingle of a limb waking up.

clue.text: Archer's fleece — popular with gangster?

parts.note: to fleece someone is to rob them
in means fashionable or popular
hood is short for hoodlum, a gangster

explanation.surface: A bowman's swindle goes down well with the mob.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary English outlaw of Sherwood Forest was a famous bowman.

clue.text: Overtake dangerously when upset

definitions.meaning: to pull in sharply in front of another vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb for swerving in front of a car, and also a colloquial adjective for distressed.

clue.text: Shrewd to ignore right of course

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub or ignore them

indicators.note: the right-hand end of a written word is its last letter, so only the final letter of course is taken

explanation.surface: Being clever enough to skip the right side of a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever or sharp-witted in a calculating way, an older sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Creatures shown by navy netted by cousin at sea

indicators.note: something netted is caught inside, so one piece goes into another
at sea means confused, so the letters of cousin are mixed up

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Sailors caught by a relative while on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'navy' as a colour or a fleet, but it is the Royal Navy abbreviation sitting inside the rearranged relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythical horned horses are creatures, an example of the class.

clue.text: Perk up, seeing her dressed up leaving hotel

indicators.note: dressed up suggests rearranging, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Seeing her all dressed up makes one perk up as one leaves the hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H ('leaving hotel') from SEEING HER and rearrange the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To give vitality or spirit to something, a synonym.

clue.text: Minor problems at home with ladies?

parts.note: in means at home
a ladies is a women's public toilet, known in Britain as a public convenience

explanation.surface: Small troubles that arise at home with women about.
explanation.definitionFit: Small annoyances or hassles, a synonym in the plural.

clue.text: Performance scheduled for part of London

parts.note: an act is a turn on stage
an event that is on is going ahead as planned

explanation.surface: A show is booked for a London venue.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTON is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a district in the west of the British capital.

clue.text: Gamble on Eire developing a particular pet hate

parts.note: a bet is a wager

indicators.note: developing means changing shape, so the letters of on and Eire are rearranged

explanation.surface: A betting habit on Ireland grows into something one loathes.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase, literally a black beast, used in English for the thing one most detests.

clue.text: Steal, but lawyers win

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers
to gain is to win or obtain

explanation.surface: Theft occurs, but the lawyers come out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A steal in the shopping sense is something bought very cheaply, a real snip.

clue.text: Draw out professional student working with force of gravity

parts.note: pro is short for professional
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates
a machine that is on is working
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A pro and a trainee work together on a physics experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw something out is to lengthen it in time, a synonym.

clue.text: Not a sad visit arranged for especially talented people

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trip that wasn't gloomy is organised for gifted guests.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names people with a striking specific gift, often alongside learning difficulties.

clue.text: Plan to put treasure under layers of rock

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits under the first

parts.note: strata are geological layers
a gem is a treasure

explanation.surface: A scheme to bury jewels beneath the rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cunning scheme or ploy, a synonym.

clue.text: Lent a hand when changing sides takes time

parts.note: as can mean when

indicators.note: to take something in is to contain it, so one letter goes inside
changing means altering, so the letters of sides are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone helped out when switching sides took a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' makes SISED from SIDES; 'takes' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Helped, the past tense, as in giving help.

clue.text: Long to take in topless joint — it's spotless

indicators.note: taking in is containing, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to pine is to long for

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, the first letter

parts.note: the wrist is a joint

explanation.surface: Yearning for a topless bar, it's absolutely clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a bar or a cannabis cigarette in the surface; here it is a body joint losing its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Immaculate, unmarked, in perfect original condition.

clue.text: Almost certain — putting a coat on and giving up

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: sure means certain
rendering is applying a coat of plaster to a wall

explanation.surface: A painter, almost certain of the job, puts a coat on and then gives up.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielding or capitulating, a synonym in the present participle.

clue.text: Delayed by father's sense of taste

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
late means delayed

explanation.surface: Dad being late affects one's appreciation of food.
explanation.definitionFit: The roof of the mouth, figuratively the ability to judge flavours.

clue.text: Extremely happy and rational over such mammals

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters
in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: sane means rational

explanation.surface: Animals that seem exceptionally happy and level-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition leans on the surface: laughing animals of Africa are such happy-seeming mammals.

clue.text: Locked up right person with secret information

parts.note: inside is slang for in prison

explanation.surface: A jailed person turns out to know secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone within an organisation who knows its private facts.

clue.text: Non-conformist bishop in dance

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a reel is a Scottish dance
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A dissenting churchman takes part in a jig.
explanation.walkthrough: Nonconformist with a capital N is a Protestant dissenter, a churchly misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who defies convention or authority.

clue.text: Those people must accept charge for treatment

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: they means those people
a rap is a criminal charge, as in take the rap

explanation.surface: People in trouble must face a charge before they can get help.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial care for a mental or physical condition.

clue.text: Travel essential for hire, including one catch

indicators.note: including means containing, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to let means available to rent
I is the Roman numeral one
to bag something is to catch it

explanation.surface: Something to rent that comes with a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travel essential' points to an item packed for a trip, here a wash bag for toiletries.
explanation.definitionFit: A wash bag is something packed for any trip.

clue.text: The links or the range?

definitions.meaning: a series of connected rings or links
a line of mountains, such as a mountain range

explanation.definitionFit: Both a series of connected rings and a line of mountains bear this name.

clue.text: Couple about to give birth stay without influence

parts.note: a pregnant woman is due when the birth is near

indicators.note: without means lacking, so letters are taken away from the word stay

parts.note: to have a say is to have influence

explanation.surface: A pregnant couple decide to stay out of anyone's influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes SAY from STAY, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece for two performers, or any pair, is a duo.

clue.text: Excited stars model for great artists

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Thrilled celebrities pose for famous painters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent European painters from before about 1800, or their works.
